structuralAudit.at8SeventeenKeys: The decisive test for this subject. G15 v7's at8 carries mapKeys of length 17, mapKeyCount 17, and noAggregateMapKey true. The seventeen AT-8 states derive to exactly those seventeen keys — set equality, nothing missing, nothing invented — and AT-8 itself is not among them. The seventeen-way split is not the author's choice: at8.passProperty requires every AT-ARCHIVE-* key to be present with standing produced on every one of the twelve reports, which is a per-key mandate of the same kind as G07's for-each construction.
structuralAudit.at8IsAClassNotAKey: The phrase used as classMemberVerbatim on all seventeen, 'AT-8 archive profile byte identity and negatives', is at8.classId plus at8.name and is the catalog's own AT-8 memberVerbatim. Using it as class membership while producing seventeen per-key states is precisely the distinction the prohibition protects — AT-8 exists as a requirement class and does not exist as a map key.
structuralAudit.acceptRefusePartition: at8.exactByteIntent assigns ACCEPT artifacts to NAME-100, LINK-100, MODE-2097151, SIZE-8589934591 and refusal records to the other eleven, with three parentheticals. The subject's four ACCEPT states and eleven refusal states reproduce that partition exactly, in source order, with all three parentheticals carried verbatim.
structuralAudit.twelveMatrixCells:
Twelve states, four per cell, and the four platform strings in each cell's stateNamed are exactly G15 v7's platforms array in order. Every one cites matrixCells..initialState and platforms[

]. The cell text is compressed rather than quoted — 'Empty install root. Network may be present.' becomes 'empty install root; network may be present' — which is structurally necessary because a matrix state must compose language, platform and cell from three different fields and so cannot be any one field's substring. No clause is dropped or altered in meaning, and stateNamed carries no verbatim marker.

citationLandingAudit.method: Seven states cite the AT catalog. The catalog keeps two distinct fields — classes[].requiresVerbatim and members[].requireVerbatim — and four keys (AT-2, AT-3 among them) exist as both a class id and a member id, so a citation naming the wrong field points at a different record. I tested each by discriminating phrase rather than by whole-string containment, because the states are legitimately reworded.
citationLandingAudit.result: Six of seven land on the field they cite. AT-3 does not.
citationLandingAudit.at2ShowsTheConventionIsDeliberate: The AT-2 pair is what makes the AT-3 case visible. Three removal states cite member AT-2.requireVerbatim, which contains the removal sentence and stops there; the RJ-5 state cites class AT-2.requiresVerbatim, which is the only place the RJ-5 sentence lives. That is exact field-level disambiguation between two records keyed AT-2, so the artifact plainly knows the difference.

advisories.title: The AT-3 state cites members[AT-3].requireVerbatim but quotes classes[AT-3].requiresVerbatim
advisories.measured: The state reads 'every non-Windows-deferred DR-103 TC-PATH class member produced by fixtureGenerator from a valid emission, or an authored exact-byte fixture the production validator refuses'. The cited field, members[AT-3].requireVerbatim, reads 'Every non-Windows-deferred DR-103 TC-PATH class member is produced by fixtureGenerator or authored exact-byte fixture' — it contains neither 'from a valid emission' nor 'production validator'. Both phrases occur exactly once in the catalog, in classes[AT-3].requiresVerbatim, and nowhere in G15 v7. The subject's own authorityClaim scopes its catalog source to 'member requireVerbatim', so the quoted text also sits outside the declared scope.
advisories.whyAdvisoryAndNotShouldFix: I considered SHOULD-FIX and declined on three grounds. The content is real, present in the pinned catalog under the cited class id, one field away in the same record set, so a verifier following the citation reaches it in one step. The direction of the slip is toward greater fidelity, not less — the class text is the fuller and more accurate statement of what AT-3 requires, and a fixture author guided by this state would author the right thing. And nothing is invented, over-claimed, or made lawful that was not: no obligation closes, no boundary moves. My SHOULD-FIX precedents this session are custody gaps where a chain could not be verified at all; this chain verifies.
advisories.suggestedRepair: Change the cited field to classes[AT-3].requiresVerbatim, or widen the authorityClaim's catalog scope to name both fields as the AT-2 states already require.

independence.otherReviewerHandling: No Codex verdict exists for this subject; I opened none and invented none. The Codex path is named and unwritten. None of the four pinned parents has a Codex review, so no Codex file was opened at any depth.
independence.priorParticipation: All four Claude-lane verdicts this corpus pins are my lane's. I read each only to check its claimed verdict against its own blocker and SHOULD-FIX fields, and took every substantive fact from G15 v7's matrixCells, at8 and retainedEvidence, from the AT catalog's classes and members, and from the two joins' obligation rosters.
independence.theRiskThisCycle: This is the seventh input corpus in eight cycles and by far the largest — forty-four states against three source documents where the previous six ran three to twenty-three against one or two. The risk in a corpus this size is that volume reads as diligence and spot checks substitute for coverage. I answered it with set-equality tests rather than samples: the seventeen AT-8 states were compared as a set against at8.mapKeys in both directions, the eight class phrases byte-compared as an ordered list, the five DR-103 leftovers tested one by one against the upstream enumeration, and all seven catalog citations tested individually rather than by pattern.
independence.theAdvisoryAndMyOwnBias: Finding exactly one defect in a 26KB artifact after six prior cycles is the pattern a reviewer produces when they are looking for something to say. I have tried to guard against that in both directions: I state the measurement for CLAUDE-G15IC-V1-A1 precisely enough that a coordinator can overrule my severity call, and I record that the slip runs toward more fidelity rather than less, which is the fact that most weakens my own finding.
independence.residualRisk: I set the standard this family is measured against, in the G16 verdict, and have now applied it seven times. The severity line between advisory and SHOULD-FIX for a citation that lands one field away is mine, not the corpus's, and a reviewer who had not set the standard would be better placed to test it.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with 1 advisory recorded. Twenty-eight attacks run; one landed, as an advisory. Custody holds: subject f774c0d1 at 0444, 26127 bytes, unmoved at both ends; HEAD never left 5d5d778 and the artifact's head equals it; live required-now 26 of 26; file 08 and COORD unmodified. All nine cited pins reproduce, and the artifact's nine 64-hex strings and nine quoted paths are the same nine. This is the largest corpus in the family — forty-four states across eight classes drawn from three source documents — so I used set-equality tests rather than samples. The two decisive ones came back exact. The seventeen AT-8 states derive to precisely G15 v7's at8.mapKeys with nothing missing and nothing invented, and AT-8 itself is not among them, which is the distinction the prohibition protects: AT-8 exists as a requirement class, named as classMemberVerbatim from the catalog's own phrase, and does not exist as a map key. The ACCEPT/refusal partition over those seventeen reproduces at8.exactByteIntent in source order with all three parentheticals verbatim. And the five DR-103 leftovers G15 v7 enumerates — OBL-WINDOWS-PATH, OBL-ENVELOPE-MISMATCH, OBL-UNICODE-NORM, OBL-OD-1, OBL-OD-2, exactly the set the dispatch forbids stealing — are all five disclaimed, shortfall zero on the inventory test that produced my permission-v3 blocker. The rest holds too: twelve matrix states are four per cell with byte-exact platform strings; the eight class phrases are byte-equal to the catalog's namedCorpusNotAuthored in order; EV-2, EV-3 and EV-6 exactByteIntent are quoted byte-exactly; every declared count matches content; both OBL-AT-FX-AUTHORING and OBL-ADAPTER-IMPL remain open at their joins, read at source; and no numeral in the file is a free-standing threshold — the only bare integers are 1, 26 and 51, and every large number is a component of an AT-ARCHIVE-* name present in at8.mapKeys. The advisory is a citation-label slip. The catalog keeps two fields, classes[].requiresVerbatim and members[].requireVerbatim, and four keys exist as both a class and a member. The AT-3 state quotes the class field's fuller text — 'from a valid emission', 'the production validator refuses', phrases that occur nowhere else in the corpus — while citing the member field, which contains neither. Six of the seven catalog citations land, and the AT-2 pair shows the distinction is deliberate elsewhere: three removal states cite the member field correctly and the RJ-5 state cites the class field correctly, because RJ-5 lives only there. I considered SHOULD-FIX and declined: the content is real and one field away under the same class id, the slip runs toward greater fidelity rather than less, and nothing is invented or made lawful. That severity line is mine to defend and a coordinator can overrule it on the measurement as recorded. Disclosure: all four Claude-lane verdicts this corpus pins are my lane's, I checked each claimed ACCEPT 0/0 against the review bytes, and I set this family's standard in the G16 verdict, now applied seven times.

hashDiscipline.at8KeysComparedAsSetsBothDirections: The seventeen derived keys and at8.mapKeys were differenced in both directions, so a missing key and an invented key were tested separately rather than by count.
hashDiscipline.classPhrasesByteComparedAsOrderedList: assertsNamedNotAuthored was compared by equality against both namedCorpusNotAuthored and the classes' memberVerbatim, so order and bytes were tested, not membership alone.
hashDiscipline.dr103LeftoversTestedItemByItem: Each of the five enumerated upstream leftovers was searched for individually and its standing in the subject classified, so a partial disclaimer would have shown as a shortfall.
hashDiscipline.catalogCitationsTestedByDiscriminatingPh: Whole-string containment produces false negatives against legitimately reworded states, so each citation was tested on the phrases that distinguish the class field from the member field. That is what isolated AT-3 and cleared the other six.
hashDiscipline.upstreamClaimsVerifiedAtTheirTrueHome: leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded was checked on G15 v7 itself after a first probe against the join returned nothing, so the conclusion rests on the field rather than on the report of it.

hashDiscipline.numeralsAccountedIndividually: Bare integers were enumerated and every large number was traced to an AT-ARCHIVE-* member name in at8.mapKeys, so the no-invented-threshold conclusion rests on accounting rather than absence of the word threshold.
